Multitaper Spectrum for Irregularly Sampled or Gappy Series (Chave 2019)

SpecMTMChave.Rd

Multitaper spectral estimate for irregularly sampled series, or regularly sampled series with gaps, after Chave (2019), using a non-uniform FFT and Slepian tapers computed for the actual sample times. The method is implemented in the Julia package Multitaper.jl (Haley and Geoga 2020), whose mdmultispec() function is called here via JuliaConnectoR. Pass either a ts (optionally with NAs, for a gappy-regular series) or a raw value vector plus explicit times (for an irregular series).

Usage

SpecMTMChave(
  x,
  times = NULL,
  deltat = 1,
  nw = 4,
  k = 7,
  nz = 0,
  detrend = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A ts object (possibly with NAs) or, if times is given, a numeric vector of values.

times

Optional numeric vector of sample times, the same length as x, for an irregular series. If NULL, the times and missing values are taken from the ts.

deltat

The nominal sample spacing, used to scale the time axis (Nyquist is 1 / (2 * deltat)). For an irregular series use e.g. the mean time step. Ignored for the ts method in the sense that the time axis is taken from the ts itself; see Details.

nw

A positive double, the time-bandwidth product (default 4). The mdmultispec bandwidth is bw = nw / N with N the number of observations, matching Thomson's \(NW = bandwidth \times N\) convention.

k

A positive integer, the number of Slepian tapers (default 7).

nz

Zero-padding factor passed to mdmultispec().

detrend

logical; remove a linear trend (against times) before estimating the spectrum. Default FALSE: detrend the series beforehand if required.

Value

A spec object with freq, spec and dof. The zero frequency is dropped. Degrees of freedom are estimated adaptively by Julia and capped at 2 * k.

Details

mdmultispec() evaluates its non-uniform FFT over \((-\pi, \pi)\) with the times used as given, and its taper bandwidth is in cycles per time unit, so the times must be in units of the nominal sample spacing (Nyquist = 0.5 cycles per unit). The times are therefore rescaled to units of deltat, the estimate is made with dt = 1 and the frequencies and spectrum are converted back to the original time units. For an irregular series pass deltat = the nominal spacing (e.g. the mean time step).

The degrees of freedom are capped because k tapers can give at most 2 * k; mdmultispec's adaptive-weight estimate can greatly exceed that where the spectrum is large relative to the series variance (up to about 1e6 has been seen), which makes FilterSpec build enormous prior filters and run very slowly.

Requires Julia, the JuliaConnectoR R package and the Julia Multitaper package:

  1. Install Julia from https://julialang.org/downloads/

  2. Install the JuliaConnectoR R package: install.packages("JuliaConnectoR")

  3. Install the Julia Multitaper package (once per Julia installation):

    JuliaConnectoR::juliaEval(
      'using Pkg; Pkg.add("Multitaper")'
    )

The Julia module is imported once per R session and cached.

Credit

The spectral estimator is the work of the authors of the Julia package Multitaper.jl, Charlotte L. Haley and Christopher J. Geoga (https://github.com/lootie/Multitaper.jl, GPL-2); this function is only a wrapper that calls it. If you use it, please cite Haley and Geoga (2020) as requested by the package, and Chave (2019) for the method.

References

Chave, A. D. (2019). Multitaper spectral analysis for irregularly sampled and gappy data. Geophysical Journal International, 218(3), 2165-2178. doi:10.1093/gji/ggz280

Haley, C. L. and Geoga, C. J. (2020). Multitaper.jl: A Julia package for frequency domain analysis of time series. Journal of Open Source Software, 5(55), 2463. doi:10.21105/joss.02463

Author

Andrew Dolman

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(42)
N <- 1000
x_full <- ts(SimPLS(N, beta = 1, alpha = 1))

# Spectrum from the complete series
sp_full <- SpecMTMChave(x_full, nw = 2, k = 3)

# Insert 20% random gaps
set.seed(7)
x_gap <- x_full
x_gap[sample(N, size = 0.2 * N)] <- NA
sp_gap <- SpecMTMChave(x_gap, nw = 2, k = 3)

# An irregularly sampled series with explicit times
t_irr <- sort(runif(N, 0, N))
sp_irr <- SpecMTMChave(as.numeric(x_full), times = t_irr,
                       deltat = mean(diff(t_irr)), nw = 2, k = 3)

gg_spec(list(`full series` = sp_full, `20% gaps` = sp_gap))
} # }
